question: In the year 1946, a three-tiered confederation for transfer of power to India was proposed by the ________.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cabinet Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cabinet Mission** was a group of high-ranking members from the British government sent to India in **1946**.
 
• Its primary objective was to discuss and plan for the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• The Mission proposed a **three-tiered confederation** consisting of provinces grouped into three sections: **Group A (Hindus majority provinces), Group B (Muslim majority provinces), and Group C (the princely states)**.
 
• This structure aimed to address the interests of various groups and provide a framework for a united yet flexible governance system.
 
• The Cabinet Mission's plan was ultimately rejected by the Muslim League, leading to further negotiations and eventually the partition of India in **1947**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulating Act**__

 __
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a system of dual control, with both the company and the British government involved in administration.
 
• This act marked the beginning of British parliamentary control over India.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act**__
 __
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, also known as the **Black Act**, was passed in 1919 by the British Government in India.
 
• It allowed the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• This act led to widespread anger and protests, including the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**__
 
 
• The **Simon Commission** was a group of seven British Members of Parliament that was sent to India in 1927 to study constitutional reform.
 
• It was met with strong opposition from Indian leaders because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The slogan "**Simon Go Back**" was popular during the protests against the commission.
